sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV

verification.notes: Section CXV: Vyasa's boon to Gandhari produces a ball of flesh divided into a hundred and one parts; Duryodhana is the first born from among these pieces, unto Dhritarashtra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV

verification.notes: Section CXV: Duryodhana is born from the ball of flesh produced in Gandhari's womb by Vyasa's boon, the first of her hundred sons.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Vaisampayana lists Vikarna among the hundred sons born to Dhritarashtra and Gandhari from the divided ball of flesh.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Vikarna is named in the roll of Gandhari's hundred sons by Dhritarashtra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Durmukha appears in Vaisampayana's roll-call of the hundred sons born to Dhritarashtra and Gandhari, in order of birth.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Durmukha is named among Gandhari's hundred sons in the birth-order list.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva, Section CLXXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXXVIII: Dhrishtadyumna names Chitrasena among 'the mighty sons of Dhritarashtra' who came with Duryodhana and Karna to Draupadi's swayamvara.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva, Section CLXXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXXVIII names Chitrasena among the sons of Dhritarashtra; as Dhritarashtra's chief queen and mother of his hundred sons per Section CXV-CXVII, Gandhari is his mother by the same lineage.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV
Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII names Duhsasana second in the birth-order roll of Dhritarashtra's hundred sons by Gandhari; Section CXV recounts the boon that produced them.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Duhsasana is named in the roll of Gandhari's hundred sons, immediately after Duryodhana and Yuyutsu.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVI
Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVI: Vyasa sets aside one extra part of the flesh-mass, over and above the hundred, to grow into a daughter for Gandhari; Section CXVII names her Duhsala and records Dhritarashtra giving her in marriage to Jayadratha.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVI

verification.notes: Section CXVI: Gandhari wishes for a daughter in addition to her hundred sons, and Vyasa sets apart one extra portion of the ball of flesh which develops into Duhsala.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV

verification.notes: Section CXV: during Gandhari's pregnancy, Dhritarashtra begets Yuyutsu on a Vaisya maidservant who attended him; Yuyutsu is named as this son.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Duryodhana and Duhsasana are both listed in birth order among the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Duryodhana and Vikarna appear together in the birth-order roll of Dhritarashtra's sons by Gandhari.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVI
Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVI-CXVII: Duhsala is born from the flesh-mass alongside Duryodhana and his brothers, as Gandhari's only daughter.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV

verification.notes: Section CXV: Yuyutsu, begotten by Dhritarashtra on a Vaisya woman during Gandhari's pregnancy, is counted among Dhritarashtra's sons alongside Duryodhana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Durmukha is listed with Duryodhana among the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra born in the same birth event.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva, Section CLXXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXXVIII: Chitrasena is named alongside Duryodhana among 'the mighty sons of Dhritarashtra' who attended Draupadi's swayamvara.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Duhsasana and Vikarna are both named among the hundred sons of Dhritarashtra and Gandhari.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVI
Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVI-CXVII: Duhsala, Gandhari's daughter, is born of the same flesh-mass as her hundred brothers including Vikarna.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXV

verification.notes: Section CXV: Yuyutsu, son of Dhritarashtra by a Vaisya woman, and Duhsasana, son of Dhritarashtra by Gandhari, are both counted among Dhritarashtra's sons born around the same time.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: 'king Dhritarashtra also bestowed Duhsala, in proper time and with proper rites, upon Jayadratha (the king of Sindhu).'

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXVII

verification.notes: Section CXVII: Jayadratha, king of Sindhu, receives Duhsala in marriage from her father Dhritarashtra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII: 'this was, without doubt, the secret known to the Sun, viz., begot by himself on Kunti, Karna was being reared in the race of the Sutas.'

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII narrates that Radha's adopted infant, found adrift on the Ganga by Adhiratha, was Kunti's (Pritha's) own son by the Sun, kept secret from all but the Sun himself.

note.en: Duryodhana makes Karna king of Anga at the tournament and the two become inseparable allies against the Pandavas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIX

verification.notes: Section CXXXIX: Duryodhana crowns Karna king of Anga on the spot, defending his unknown birth against Bhima's taunts, and 'the heroic Karna, accomplished in arms, began to gratify Duryodhana by sweet speeches' -- the founding scene of their lifelong friendship and alliance.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIX

verification.notes: Section CXXXIX: Karna, having been crowned king of Anga by Duryodhana, 'became intent on injuring the sons of Pritha' out of loyalty to his benefactor and friend.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII: Adhiratha sent Karna to Hastinapura where 'Karna put up with Drona, for the purpose of learning arms,' and 'having acquired all the four kinds of weapons from Drona, Kripa, and Rama, he became famous in the world as a mighty bowman.'

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII: Karna trains under Drona alongside the princes of the Kuru house before contracting his friendship with Duryodhana.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII states Karna 'acquired all the four kinds of weapons from Drona, Kripa, and Rama' -- Rama here being Rama Jamadagnya (Parashurama), from whom Karna later separately obtains the Brahmastra before being cursed by him.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVII

verification.notes: Section CCCVII lists Rama (Parashurama) among the three masters -- Drona, Kripa, and Rama -- from whom Karna acquired his mastery of weapons.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva, Section CLXXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXXVIII names 'Sakuni, Sauvala, Vrisaka, and Vrihadvala -- these sons of the king Gandhara' among the assembled princes at Draupadi's swayamvara, establishing Shakuni as a son of the Gandhara royal house into which Gandhari, Dhritarashtra's queen, was also born.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Swayamvara Parva, Section CLXXXVIII

verification.notes: Section CLXXXVIII names Sakuni among the sons of the king of Gandhara, the same royal house of Gandhari's birth, establishing him as her brother.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVIII

verification.notes: Section CCCVIII: Indra, disguised as a Brahmana, trades Karna a dart 'incapable of being baffled' for his natural armor and earrings; Karna accepts, calling it the Vasavi dart, and is told he may hurl it only once, in mortal peril.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Vana Parva, Aranya Parva, Section CCCVIII

verification.notes: Section CCCVIII: Indra gives Karna the dart in exchange for his coat of mail and earrings, warning him it will slay only one enemy and then return to Indra's hand.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Karna Parva, Section XC
Karna Parva, Section XCI

verification.notes: Section XC: 'the earth swallowed up one of wheels of Karna's car'; Section XCI: 'Cut off with the Anjalika weapon in that battle, the head of Karna fell down along with his body' -- Arjuna beheads Karna after his chariot wheel sinks into the ground during their final duel.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Karna Parva, Section XCI

verification.notes: Section XCI: Arjuna severs Karna's head with the Anjalika weapon while Karna's chariot wheel is stuck in the earth and Karna struggles to free it, ending the Kurukshetra war's central duel between the two rivals.

note.en: Bhima kills Duhsasana at Kurukshetra, drinking his blood in fulfilment of his dice-hall vow.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Karna Parva, Section LXXXIII

verification.notes: Section LXXXIII: Bhima fells Duhsasana with his mace, cuts open his breast, drinks his blood, and beheads him, fulfilling the vow he swore in the dice hall after Draupadi's disrobing.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Karna Parva, Section LXXXIII

verification.notes: Section LXXXIII: Duhsasana is slain by Bhima, who drinks his blood on the battlefield, avenging the assembly-hall humiliation of Draupadi.

note.en: Bhima kills Duryodhana by breaking his thighs with his mace, fulfilling his dice-hall vow.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Shalya Parva, Gada Yuddha Parva, Section LX

verification.notes: Section LX: 'Formerly Bhima had vowed in the midst of the assembly that he would in great battle break with his mace the thighs of Duryodhana' -- Bhima strikes Duryodhana down by shattering his thighs with his mace in their final duel.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Shalya Parva, Gada Yuddha Parva, Section LX

verification.notes: Section LX: Duryodhana is struck down by Bhima, who breaks his thighs with the mace as vowed after the dice-hall humiliation of Draupadi.

note.en: Yuyutsu, Dhritarashtra's son by a Vaisya woman, defects from Duryodhana's army to fight for the Pandavas just before the war begins.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Bhishma Parva, Section XLIII

verification.notes: Section XLIII: on the eve of battle, Yuyutsu abandons his Kaurava brothers and joins the Pandavas -- 'Yuyutsu then, abandoning the Kurus thy sons, went over to the army of the Pandavas' -- the decisive break between him and Duryodhana's cause.

note.en: Shakuni, master of loaded dice, wins the fateful game against Yudhishthira on Duryodhana's behalf, engineering the Pandavas' exile.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Sabha Parva, Section LXVI

verification.notes: Section LXVI: at the dice game staged for Duryodhana's benefit, onlookers say 'Sakuni hath played with him deceitfully,' describing Shakuni's loaded dice defeating Yudhishthira on Duryodhana's behalf.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLV

verification.notes: Section CXLV: guided by Krishna's ruse of the false sunset, Arjuna looses a mantra-inspired arrow that 'snatched Jayadratha's head away' and carried it to fall in his father Vriddhakshatra's lap, fulfilling Arjuna's vow to slay him before sunset.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Drona Parva, Jayadratha-vadha Parva, Section CXLV

verification.notes: Section CXLV: Jayadratha, king of Sindhu and husband of Duhsala, is beheaded by Arjuna after the Pandava army corners him at day's end during the search for Abhimanyu's killers.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIV

verification.notes: Section CXXXIV: Bhishma gives the Kaurava and Pandava princes to Drona as pupils; 'two of Drona's pupils became very much accomplished in the use of mace. These were Duryodhana and Bhima.'

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Adi Parva, Sambhava Parva, Section CXXXIV

verification.notes: Section CXXXIV: Duryodhana trains under Drona together with his brothers and cousins, becoming especially skilled with the mace.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Uluka Dutagamana Parva, Section CLXI

verification.notes: Section CLXI (titled 'Uluka Dutagamana Parva'): Duryodhana summons Uluka, addressed as 'son of an adept at dice' (Shakuni's son), and sends him as an envoy to deliver a defiant message to the Pandavas on the eve of the Kurukshetra war.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Uluka Dutagamana Parva, Section CLXI

verification.notes: Section CLXI: Duryodhana, having consulted with Karna, Duhsasana, and Shakuni, privately briefs Uluka and dispatches him as his herald to taunt the Pandavas into battle.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Uluka Dutagamana Parva, Section CLXI

verification.notes: Section CLXI: before sending Uluka as envoy, 'king Duryodhana... summoned those rulers of men, viz., Karna and Dussasana and Sakuni, the son of Suvala, and began... to consult with them,' showing Shakuni as one of Duryodhana's inner war council.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Uluka Dutagamana Parva, Section CLXI

verification.notes: Section CLXI: Shakuni is one of the three counsellors -- with Karna and Duhsasana -- whom Duryodhana consults before opening hostilities with his message to the Pandavas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Uluka Dutagamana Parva, Section CLXI

verification.notes: Section CLXI: Duryodhana consults his brother Duhsasana together with Karna and Shakuni as his closest war council on the eve of Kurukshetra.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Bhagwat Yana Parva, Section CXLIV
Udyoga Parva, Bhagwat Yana Parva, Section CXLV

verification.notes: Section CXLIV-CXLV: on the eve of war, Kunti goes to the Ganga and reveals to Karna that she is his mother and Surya his father, urging him to join his brothers the Pandavas.

sources.source_chapter_or_section: Udyoga Parva, Bhagwat Yana Parva, Section CXLVI

verification.notes: Section CXLVI: Karna, though confirming he now knows Kunti is his mother, refuses to abandon Duryodhana out of gratitude, but grants her the boon that he will spare Yudhishthira, Bhima, Nakula, and Sahadeva in battle and fight only Arjuna -- 'the number of thy sons will never be less than five.'
